subject: HyperDrive tri-region capacity onboarding request and timeline
messages:
From: Aisha Gupta <aisha@hyperdrive.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@hyperdrive.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood intro — capacity ask for initial pilot (tri-region)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. HyperDrive is moving fast and wants to include Redwood as the inference backbone for an upcoming pilot across US/EU/APAC. We sketched rough expected traffic in the attached spreadsheet (hyperdrive_capacity_needs_v1.xlsx) — it includes token/sec estimates, peak concurrency windows, and model choices (gpt-small variants and a trimmed 13B).

Key asks: can Redwood commit a tri-region dedicated footprint (US+EU+APAC) for a 6-month pilot with predictable latency targets (p95 < 120ms for US/EU, < 200ms APAC) and an onramp schedule that gets APAC online in week 6? Procurement asked for an SOW and a rough timeline to share with their legal team.

Can you put together a short capacity proposal and an initial SOW draft?

Appreciate it — Aisha

--
Aisha Gupta
Head of Platform Integrations, HyperDrive
A: hyperdrive.ai

Attachment: hyperdrive_capacity_needs_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: HyperDrive tri-region capacity onboarding request and timeline

Team — forwarding HyperDrive's ask. Quick summary: pilot to run 6 months, wants tri-region dedicated capacity, strict p95 latency targets, APAC needs to be live by week 6. Attached is their demand spreadsheet.

Immediate questions we need to answer for a first-pass response to Aisha: 1) realistic GPU pool sizing by region for their token/sec / concurrency profiles, 2) an onramp timeline with gating milestones (SOW sign, network setup, certs, pilot cutover), 3) any hard blockers for APAC week-6 onboard (capacity, procurement, or customs).

I can own the SOW draft and customer-facing timeline. Rishi — can you run a sizing estimate (GPU counts, estimated reserved slots) and a short note on possible latency vs model/quantization tradeoffs? Vanessa — can you flag any compliance/residency items for EU/APAC that will affect timeline? Lauren — I'll need a blunt ops readiness ETA for provisioning (how long until we can carve a dedicated pool in each region and tests needed).

For replies: keep them short (we'll assemble a one-pager).

Thanks,
Jonas

Attachment: hyperdrive_capacity_needs_v1.xlsx (forwarded)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: HyperDrive tri-region capacity onboarding request and timeline

All — I ran the numbers against their peak-concurrency rows. Notes:

- US: to meet p95 <120ms for the stated model mix (mix of 6B quant and 13B trimmed), estimated baseline reserved = 40 A100-equivalent slots (continuous) with 12 A100-equivalent burst slots for weekly peaks. That maps to ~8 racks in our US pool depending on packing.

- EU: similar mix; baseline reserved = 30 A100-eq with 8 burst slots. Expect slightly higher p95 due to inter-zone routing unless we pin to a single major EU region (Frankfurt).

- APAC: demand is lower but latency SLO is looser. Baseline reserved = 18 A100-eq with 6 burst. The tricky part is APAC provisioning timelines: procurement + customs for physical placements could add 4–8 weeks if hardware is ordered; if we use cloud-hosted specialists we can do bootstrapped onramp in ~3–4 weeks but with higher unit cost.

Tradeoffs/mitigation: aggressive quantization to 4-bit for the 13B model reduces GPU-time by ~35% but may need QA; KV-cache warmup will matter for initial cutover; we should include a short quality guardrail (eval set) in SOW.

I'll prepare a short sizing table and two ops scenarios (cloud-bootstrap vs reserved hardware) for the one-pager.

Rishi

Attachment: sizing_estimates_hyperdrive_v1.csv (calc export, 18KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: HyperDrive tri-region capacity onboarding request and timeline

Quick compliance/region notes:

- EU (Frankfurt) is fine; HyperDrive indicated no special data residency beyond standard EU controls. We'll need a data processing addendum in the SOW and SOC2 evidence (we can reference our hosted SOC2 report).

- APAC: Singapore and Tokyo are both possible. HyperDrive prefers Singapore for lower latency to SE Asia customers, but their procurement flagged potential import/customs hold-ups if physical infra is required. If they accept cloud-hosted APAC nodes (partner region), we can hit week-6. Otherwise, hardware route likely slips to week ~10–12.

- Security: need to confirm KMS integration (customer-managed keys?) — note that will affect onboarding by ~3 business days for certs and key exchange.

Vanessa

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Apr 2028 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: HyperDrive tri-region capacity onboarding request and timeline

Provisioning ETA (ops perspective):

- Cloud-bootstrap scenario (preferred for speed):
  * US pool: carve & test in 7 business days after SOW + approval + billing setup.
  * EU pool (Frankfurt): carve & test in 9 business days (inter-zone certificates add time).
  * APAC (Singapore, partner-hosted): carve & smoke-test in 12 business days.

- Dedicated hardware scenario: ordering + racking + network + certs = 6–10 weeks (APAC at upper end).

Testing checklist: deployment runbook, latency synthetic tests from target geographies, end-to-end KV-cache warmup, and perf regression run vs baseline. Ops will need two engineers for the cutover week and one week of on-call post-cutover.

I can put these into a simple SOW timeline (GANTT) and include a risk row about APAC customs.

Lauren

Attachment: ops_onboard_tasklist.txt (12KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Gupta <aisha@hyperdrive.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@hyperdrive.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Apr 2028 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HyperDrive tri-region capacity onboarding request and timeline

Aisha — thanks for the ask and the worksheet. Attached is a short one-pager summary and SOW draft for internal review (SOW-dedicated-hyperdrive-v1.pdf) plus a network sketch (cdm-network-diagram.png). Summary highlights:

- Proposed go-forward: cloud-bootstrap in APAC to meet week-6 onramp; reserved dedicated pools in US (40 A100-eq baseline + burst) and EU (30 A100-eq baseline). Estimated lead time post-SOW signature: US ~7 business days, EU ~9 business days, APAC (cloud bootstrap) ~12 business days.
- Optional hardware commit (lower unit cost) available after pilot; timeline 6–10 weeks to provision physical racks in APAC.
- We will include a short quality guardrail (eval harness + acceptance criteria) and an ops cutover runbook in the SOW.

Next steps for hyperdrive: 1) confirm APAC cloud-bootstrap is acceptable, 2) confirm whether customer-managed KMS is required, and 3) provide procurement contact for DocuSign / SOW routing. If all good I can route the SOW to Procurement and Legal for redlines.

If you want, we can schedule a 30m alignment tomorrow for the timeline and acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Jonas

Attachment: SOW-dedicated-hyperdrive-v1.pdf (draft, 68KB); cdm-network-diagram.png (image, 25KB)
